reasoning: As of March 6, 2026, the March 17-18 FOMC meeting is imminent (11-12 days away). To forecast whether there will be no change in Fed rates, I need to consider: (1) Recent economic conditions and inflation trends through early March 2026, (2) Fed communication patterns, (3) Historical frequency of rate changes at FOMC meetings. Without real-time data, I rely on typical patterns: the Fed generally signals major policy shifts in advance, and emergency rate changes between meetings are rare. If a change were planned, it would likely have been signaled. The proximity to the meeting means market expectations are largely set. Given that most FOMC meetings result in no change (the Fed typically moves in deliberate steps with clear communication), and absent indication of an emergency situation, the baseline probability of no change is moderately high, though not overwhelming.
